apps.name: Ryujinx-Nextendo
apps.release_notes:
## Mario Tennis Aces and ARMS join the network

Both games are now recognised by Nextendo and can be launched straight into online play.
As with every other supported title, one game version is supported at a time — **ARMS
5.5.1** and **Mario Tennis Aces 3.1.1**, both the latest. If your copy is on an older
version, Nextendo now tells you before launch instead of letting you walk into a
connection error with no explanation.

## Mario Tennis Aces picks the closest server for you

Tennis leans on peer-to-peer far more than the other titles, and players on the far side
of the world were paying for it. The game now resolves a real GeoDNS name instead of a
fixed address, so you are routed to whichever of the two live Tennis nodes is nearest —
one in Europe, one in North America. Every other game is untouched.

This is a first step, not the destination: the two nodes are separate for now, and
cross-node play is what comes next. If you would rather stay on the European node, set
`NEXTENDO_TENNIS_GEODNS=0` and the previous behaviour comes back. Running your own
private server? The redirect never applies to you — your server keeps Tennis, exactly as
it keeps everything else.

Both of the above come from **@CollectingW**, who also set up and hosts the second node.

## Splatfest data now ships with the emulator

Splatoon 3 Splatfests need a data package the console would normally receive over the
air. Until now you had to be handed that package and drop it in yourself. It is included
in this build, in `portable/bcat-seed/`, so a fresh install is ready for the event with
nothing to configure.

The package is included for all four Splatfest regions — Japan, the Americas, Europe and
Asia-Pacific — because the game asks for the one matching the region you picked in-game, and
that choice can only be changed once a month. Whichever you are on, the data is there.

Two consequences worth knowing. **The in-app updater will not put it there for you** — it
deliberately leaves your `portable` folder alone so it never touches your saves, keys or
settings. If you update from inside the emulator, extract this archive over your
installation afterwards to get the package. And if you are on macOS, the build has no
`portable` folder at all; take the separate package asset attached to this release.

## Splatoon 2 no longer wipes Splatoon 3's event data

The two games share one folder for their downloaded data, and Splatoon 2 refreshed it by
deleting the whole thing before writing its own files. Anyone who installed the Splatoon
3 event package and then launched Splatoon 2 once lost it, silently — and on a fresh
install that deletion was guaranteed on the very first launch.

Splatoon 2 now removes only the folders it owns. Nothing to do on your side: existing
installations are handled correctly from the first launch after updating.

## The console clock now follows your PC

Two settings are on by default from this release.

**Match system time** keeps the emulated console's clock on your computer's. Without it
the console clock drifts, and an event whose phases change at fixed times puts you in the
wrong one — you get the announcement while everyone else is already playing.

**Ignore missing services** lets a game continue when it asks for something the emulator
does not implement, instead of stopping. Several of those are called during online play
and their absence changes nothing.

Both were settings every online player ended up having to find on their own.

## Discord shows the right game again

Nextendo-compatible titles appear on Discord under **Ryujinx | Nextendo** rather than
plain Ryujinx. ARMS and Mario Tennis Aces were missing from the list that decides this,
so they were announced as ordinary Ryujinx sessions. Fixed, and Mario Tennis Aces now
shows its real cover art.

## Splatoon 3: an event logo on the title screen

During a Splatfest, the Splatoon 3 title screen can now show the event's logo instead of
the usual one. The server decides — nothing to install, nothing to toggle, and when the
event ends the title screen returns to normal on its own.

Worth saying plainly, because Splatoon 3 otherwise allows no mods at all: **nothing is
added to your game**. Nintendo shipped several logos inside the title screen file already;
the emulator simply serves a different one, in memory, while the game loads. Your files are
never modified and no game data is distributed. If the server says nothing, or cannot be
reached, the title screen is left completely untouched.


## Downloads

| Platform | File |
|---|---|
| Windows x64 | `Nextendo-1.7.9-win-x64.zip` |
| Linux x64 | `Nextendo-1.7.9-linux-x64.tar.gz` |
| macOS (universal) | `Ryujinx-Nextendo-1.7.9-macos_universal.tar.gz` |
| Splatfest package (all regions) | `bcat-seed-JUEA-00210.zip` |

Extract the archive and keep the `portable` folder next to the executable — that is where
your saves, keys and settings live.

Updating from inside the emulator? Extract the archive over your installation afterwards,
or take the Splatfest package on its own — the in-app updater never writes into `portable`.

apps.name: eden-stable
apps.release_notes:
## Changelog

This is a hotfix release for 0.2.0, addressing some crashes and bugs that occurred in certain situations. CPU and graphics performance will remain largely the same.

This release does *not* use SDL3, and remains on SDL2.

# Universal

- The Windows auto updater now accounts for the current build ID and will properly fetch the corresponding build to your currently installed Eden
- Fixed crashes and errors that could occur when large amounts of games and external content files were present
- Fixed crashes on 12th-gen Intel CPUs
- Fixed MK8DX freeze when the native controller applet was used
- Fixed a rare case of weird noises playing on shutdown
- Fixed mods that expect a real value out of `DefaultDataSpace`
- Fixed some minor issues with emulated controller thread contention

# Internal

- Fixed several build errors:
  - Newer Xbyak removed Xeon Phi features
  - Unused variable errors in NCE
  - Removed `httplib` version restrictions

# Packages

## Targets

Each build is optimized for a specific architecture and uses a specific compiler.

- **aarch64/arm64**: For devices that use the armv8-a instruction set; e.g. Snapdragon X, all Android devices, and Apple Silicon Macs.
- **amd64**: For devices that use the amd64 (aka x86_64) instruction set; this is exclusively used by Intel and AMD CPUs and is only found on desktops.
- **v3**: For devices that use the x86_64-v3 instruction set or newer; this is found on Ryzen, Intel 4th Generation (Haswell), and newer.

### PGO

PGO builds usually perform ~10-30% better than standard builds, and are thus generally recommended for all users.

## Linux

Linux packages are distributed via AppImage.
[zsync](https://zsync.moria.org.uk/) files are provided for easier updating, such as via
[AM](https://github.com/ivan-hc/AM).

| Build Type | Standard | PGO (Recommended) | Notes |
|------------|----------|-----------|-------|
| amd64 | [Standard AppImage](https://stable.eden-emu.dev/v0.2.1/Eden-Linux-v0.2.1-amd64-gcc-standard.AppImage) ([zsync](https://stable.eden-emu.dev/v0.2.1/Eden-Linux-amd64-gcc-standard.AppImage.zsync)) | [PGO AppImage](https://stable.eden-emu.dev/v0.2.1/Eden-Linux-v0.2.1-amd64-clang-pgo.AppImage) ([zsync](https://stable.eden-emu.dev/v0.2.1/Eden-Linux-amd64-clang-pgo.AppImage.zsync)) |  |

| ARM (aarch64) | [Standard AppImage](https://stable.eden-emu.dev/v0.2.1/Eden-Linux-v0.2.1-aarch64-gcc-standard.AppImage) ([zsync](https://stable.eden-emu.dev/v0.2.1/Eden-Linux-aarch64-gcc-standard.AppImage.zsync)) | [PGO AppImage](https://stable.eden-emu.dev/v0.2.1/Eden-Linux-v0.2.1-aarch64-clang-pgo.AppImage) ([zsync](https://stable.eden-emu.dev/v0.2.1/Eden-Linux-aarch64-clang-pgo.AppImage.zsync)) |  |

### Room Executables

These are statically linked Linux executables for the `eden-room` binary.

- [aarch64](https://stable.eden-emu.dev/v0.2.1/eden-room-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl)

| Zen 4 | [Standard zip](https://stable.eden-emu.dev/v0.2.1/Eden-Windows-v0.2.1-rog-ally-gcc-standard.zip) | [PGO zip](https://stable.eden-emu.dev/v0.2.1/Eden-Windows-v0.2.1-rog-ally-clang-pgo.zip) | Requires Zen 4 or newer (e.g. ROG Ally X, Legion Go S). Incompatible with Intel |
| aarch64/arm64 | [Standard zip](https://stable.eden-emu.dev/v0.2.1/Eden-Windows-v0.2.1-arm64-clang-standard.zip) | [PGO zip](https://stable.eden-emu.dev/v0.2.1/Eden-Windows-v0.2.1-arm64-clang-pgo.zip) | Snapdragon devices |

## Android

| Build  | Notes |
|--------|-------|

| [Genshin Spoof APK](https://stable.eden-emu.dev/v0.2.1/Eden-Android-v0.2.1-optimized.apk) | Spoofs Eden as Genshin Impact, which may enable optimizations/frame generation on some flagship devices. |
| [Legacy APK](https://stable.eden-emu.dev/v0.2.1/Eden-Android-v0.2.1-legacy.apk) | For Snapdragon 865 and other unsupported chipsets |

## macOS

macOS comes in a DMG image. These builds are currently experimental, and you should expect major graphical glitches and crashes.
In order to run the app, you *may* need to go to System Settings -> Privacy & Security -> Security -> Allow untrusted app.

- [macOS DMG](https://stable.eden-emu.dev/v0.2.1/Eden-macOS-v0.2.1.dmg)

## Torrent

A torrent containing all artifacts. To use this, simply download the torrent and import it into your
favorite torrent client (BitTorrent only!), and artifacts will be downloaded automatically.
- [Torrent](https://stable.eden-emu.dev/v0.2.1/Eden-v0.2.1.torrent)
